method: Native source-only annotation boards, full diagnostic stills, and an ordered contact sheet of every decoded video frame; not real-time playback.
observations: The original reflection remains on both source and fallback panels throughout.
Combined proposal masks cover only portions of visibly exposed iris and vary abruptly through the blink.
Source 977 left has almost no candidate iris and is rejected; right retains a lower crescent candidate.
Source 982 has no combined candidate on either nearly closed eye and is rejected.
Source 984 left is nearly closed but passes the experimental candidate gate: 51 iris pixels, 27 pupil pixels, offset 0.569603 px, pupil ratio 0.201855. This view cannot certify visible iris material.
Source 985 left/right retain small candidate regions but reject under the minimum iris area rule.
All six freshly marked reflections approach or overlap obscured pupil boundaries; underlying material and full reflection extent are not independently known.
post_hoc_scope: Blink findings at 982/984/985 were inspected after model outputs. They were not used to change frozen thresholds or relabel the primary evaluation.
limitations: Sparse assistant labels and contact-sheet review do not establish dense visibility, temporal tracking accuracy, clean donor support, or generalization to independent footage.
